name: The Box's Riddle (Electric Shock Trap)
trigger: Inserting the incorrect key or trying to pick the lock

detection.detail: Recognizing the shape of the dragon lock or the box's aquatic decorations as indicative of a bronze dragon; if a character saw someone get shocked by lightning after an incorrect guess, the DC for this check is reduced to 11.

disarm.detail: Inserting the correct bronze key opens the lock without triggering the trap.

effect: The lock emits an electric shock.
description: A locked wooden box with a dragon-shaped lock that shocks those who insert the wrong key or try to pick it.

name: Ghostgrass Patch
trigger: A creature tries to swim past the ghostgrass

detection.detail: The pale plants blocking the exit to the cavern are ghostgrass, a carnivorous variety of sea grass.

disarm.detail: A creature can use an action to try to free itself or another creature within its reach from the ghostgrass, doing so with a successful DC 12 Strength (Athletics) check.

effect: A creature that tries to swim past the ghostgrass must succeed on a DC 12 Dexterity saving throw or take 3 (1d6) necrotic damage and be restrained. A restrained creature takes the damage again at the start of each of its turns until it escapes.
area: A thick patch of bone-white sea grass blocking the exit to the cavern
description: A carnivorous variety of sea grass that restrains and damages creatures that fail a Dexterity save.

name: Landslide
trigger: As you swim into this area, ripples course through the water as more rocky debris begins to slide toward you.

detection.detail: One side of the chamber is covered in the crumbled and muddy remains of a landslide.

effect: Each character must make a DC 14 Dexterity saving throw, taking 10 (3d6) bludgeoning damage from the landslide on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
area: One side of the chamber covered in crumbled and muddy remains of a landslide
description: A landslide of rocky debris that damages characters who fail a Dexterity save.

name: Sacrifice Engine
trigger: A creature is in the pit while the blades are spinning

detection.detail: The pit is 30 feet deep and lined with rows of silver blades; a lever near the edge can be pulled to spin the blades.

disarm.detail: Pulling the lever near the edge of the pit stops the blades from spinning.

effect: A creature in the pit while the blades are spinning takes 44 (8d10) slashing damage at the start of each of its turns.
description: A 30-foot-deep pit lined with rows of silver blades that can be made to spin by pulling a lever near the edge.

name: Vrock Corpse Spore Eruption
trigger: A failed DC 15 Wisdom (Survival) check to extract the contents of the vrock's stomach.

detection.detail: To extract the contents of the vrock's stomach, a character must first cleave through the vrock's hide.

disarm.detail: No disarm method described; avoid triggering by succeeding on the Survival check.

effect: An eruption of spores from the vrock's corpse that fill a 10-foot-radius sphere centered on the corpse. All creatures in that area must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution saving throw or become poisoned. A creature poisoned in this way takes 5 (1d10) poison damage at the start of each of its turns. It can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
description: A failed attempt to cut open a dead vrock's stomach causes a spore eruption.

name: Bladed Corridor
trigger: Whenever one or more creatures are in the hall, the floor tilts to one side and then the other so that creatures stumble into the blades.

detection.detail: Characters who have a passive Wisdom (Perception) score of 12 or higher notice a phrase written in Undercommon on the floor between the two statues.

disarm.detail: If the crystal canister is destroyed, the characters have no way to disable the hall's trap.

effect: A creature that moves into the corridor or starts its turn there must make a DC 20 Dexterity saving throw, taking 17 (5d6) slashing damage on a failed saving throw, or half as much damage on a successful one.
area: The corridor north of the statues
description: A corridor with twitching silver blades protruding from its walls; the floor tilts to make creatures stumble into the blades.

name: Stained-Glass Mosaic Trap
trigger: A creature presses an incorrect symbol on the mosaic

detection.detail: A character who succeeds on a DC 11 Intelligence (Religion) check recognizes these as the symbols of evil gods.

disarm.method: Pressing the correct four symbols in order
disarm.detail: If four of the symbols are pressed in the correct order, as noted in the Symbol Sequence table, a door opens at the base of the wall.

effect: A creature that presses an incorrect symbol must make a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw, taking 28 (8d6) psychic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
description: A 10-foot-wide section of wall at the north end of the basilica resembles a tall, stained-glass window. Its imagery changes constantly, but nine symbols remain static. If four of the symbols are pressed in the correct order, a door opens. Pressing an incorrect symbol deals psychic damage.

name: Chains of Darkness Trap
trigger: A creature falls prone in the hall (area R10)

detection.detail: A creature that enters this hall immediately feels weighed down and senses a terrible dread. The creature must make a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw.

disarm.detail: Any creature that is not grappled by the chains can use an action to try to free a chained creature within reach, doing so with a successful DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check.

effect: The creature must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or be grappled by the chains (escape DC 15). Until it escapes, the creature takes 5 (1d10) psychic damage at the start of each of its turns. Whatever the result of the check, the creature making the attempt takes 11 (2d10) psychic damage.
damage: 5 (1d10) per turn while grappled; 11 (2d10) to the rescuer
description: When a creature falls prone in this hall, the chains on the floor slither toward it, and the figures carved in the walls drone in low voices. The creature must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or be grappled by the chains, taking psychic damage each turn.

name: Abyssal Rift
trigger: When a creature passes through the gaping mouth of the stone-carved face of Gruumsh in area R15

detection.detail: The rift is visible as a 10-foot-wide, 20-foot-long orifice filled with impenetrable darkness. Horrible shrieks emanate from it.

disarm.detail: The rift closes after 1 minute automatically. No disarm method is given.

effect: A creature that enters the rift from this side is magically transported, along with anything it is wearing or carrying, to the Abyss. The creature emerges from a similar rift located inside a colossal cyclone of poisonous gas. A creature caught in the cyclone is trapped there and takes 14 (4d6) poison damage at the start of each of its turns. A creature that has a flying speed can escape the cyclone by flying into the rift; a creature without a flying speed can use an action to try to harness the winds of the cyclone, propelling itself through the rift with a successful DC 19 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check.
description: A planar rift that opens in the floor on the east side of the chasm when a creature passes through the carving of Gruumsh's face. It is a gateway to the Abyss.

name: Vault Trap
trigger: If the vault is opened by any means other than using the master key, the vault's magical trap is triggered.

detection.detail: A character who examines the vault and succeeds on a successful DC 20 Intelligence (Investigation) check finds a thin keyhole near its base.

disarm.detail: The trap can't be disarmed, but successfully casting dispel magic (DC 15) on the lock before an attempt is made to open it suppresses the trap for 1 minute, allowing the lock to be manipulated without negative consequences.

effect: Each creature within 5 feet of the vault must make a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed saving throw, a creature takes 36 (8d8) psychic damage and is stunned for 1 minute. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage and isn't stunned.
area: Each creature within 5 feet of the vault
description: A magical trap on the casino's coin vault that triggers if opened without the master key.

name: Vault Door Energy Blast Trap
trigger: Forcing the vault door open (DC 21 Strength (Athletics) check)

detection.detail: A character who searches the basement and succeeds on a DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check notices the faint outline of a circular stone door in the wall next to a bookcase that is bolted to the floor.

disarm.detail: This trap can't be disarmed.

effect: A loud, concussive blast of energy fills a 15-foot cube immediately outside the vault. Any creature in the cube must make a DC 18 Constitution saving throw, taking 33 (6d10) thunder damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
description: A magical trap that releases a concussive blast of energy when the vault door is forced open.

name: Trapdoor (disguised as symbol of Corellon)
trigger: A character who searches the tower ruins and succeeds on a DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check discovers a large symbol of Corellon inscribed on the floor, mostly hidden under sand and debris. Closer examination discloses a 5-foot-diameter, circular stone trapdoor disguised as part of the symbol.

detection.detail: A character who searches the tower ruins and succeeds on a DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check discovers a large symbol of Corellon inscribed on the floor, mostly hidden under sand and debris. Closer examination discloses a 5-foot-diameter, circular stone trapdoor disguised as part of the symbol.

disarm.detail: The trapdoor is closed and stuck. A character can use an action to try to pry it up by using a crowbar or similar tool.

effect: The trapdoor is closed and stuck. A character can use an action to try to pry it up by using a crowbar or similar tool.
description: A stone trapdoor disguised as part of a symbol of Corellon, stuck and requiring effort to open.

name: Burst of Radiance Trap
trigger: A creature enters the armory without first saying a prayer to Corellon.

detection.detail: A character who searches the opening for traps and succeeds on a DC 17 Intelligence (Investigation) check spots a tiny glyph inscribed along the edge of the opening, in a location that's not visible while the trapdoor is closed.

disarm.method: dispel magic (DC 17) or defaced using mason's tools or similar equipment
disarm.detail: If this glyph is dispelled with a successful casting of dispel magic (DC 17) or defaced using mason's tools or similar equipment, the following trap ceases to function.

effect: A burst of radiance flares from the chamber. Each creature in the armory and within 15 feet of the trapdoor must make a DC 18 Constitution saving throw, taking 33 (6d10) radiant damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. This trap can be triggered only once.
area: The armory and within 15 feet of the trapdoor
description: A magical trap that triggers a burst of radiant damage when a creature enters the armory without praying to Corellon.

name: Secret Door (Netherdeep)
trigger: Any creature within 10 feet of a secret door that deals damage to it

detection.detail: A character who spends at least 10 minutes searching an area for secret doors can make a DC 20 Intelligence (Investigation) check at the end of that search. If the check succeeds and there's a secret door to be found, the character finds it.

disarm.detail: Secret doors in the Netherdeep are unlocked unless otherwise noted, and they open easily despite their great weight.

effect: Any creature within 10 feet of a secret door that deals damage to it must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw, taking 22 (4d10) psychic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
description: A secret door made of ruidium-veined stone that deals psychic damage to creatures that damage it.

name: Boiling Water (Vents of Fury)
trigger: If the bloodfin is killed, the vents in the floor flare with bright red light and spew forth a flood of boiling-hot water.

detection.detail: Characters who have a passive Wisdom (Perception) score of 17 or higher notice something more: At the far end of the thirty-foot-high cavern, a monstrous fish with a red-streaked body chases a school of much smaller fish.

disarm.detail: No disarm method described.

effect: Any creature that starts its turn in the boiling-hot water must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw, taking 21 (6d6) fire damage on a failed saving throw, or half as much damage on a successful one. The scalding heat lasts for 1 hour, after which the vents return to their normal illumination and the water temperature in the cavern again becomes bearably warm.
description: The bubbling columns of water rising from the vents are hot, but not hot enough to damage creatures that enter them. If the bloodfin is killed, the vents spew boiling-hot water.

name: Ruidium Spines (Current Trap)
trigger: If the characters kill the light devourer, the current intensifies for 1 hour. Until the current returns to normal, any creature that starts its turn in this chamber must succeed on a DC 14 Strength saving throw or be thrust against a wall by the current and skewered by ruidium spines.

detection.detail: The walls are lined with ruidium spines, visible to any creature entering the chamber.

disarm.detail: No disarm method described; the trap is triggered by killing the light devourer.

effect: The creature takes 5 (1d10) piercing damage from the spines and must succeed on a DC 20 Charisma saving throw or gain 1 level of exhaustion. If the creature is not already suffering from ruidium corruption, it becomes corrupted when it fails the saving throw.
description: A current threatens to pull creatures into this chamber, the walls of which are lined with ruidium spines. The Apotheon's ragged breathing is audible. Thermal vents in the floor give off swirling bubbles, dim light, and warmth.

name: Scalding Pit (Boiling Water)
trigger: If either the ruidium greatsword or the ruidium shield is removed from its resting place, the vents in the floor flare with bright red light and spew forth a flood of boiling-hot water

detection.detail: The vents in the floor are visible, but the trap is triggered by removing the items.

disarm.detail: The trap cannot be disarmed; it lasts for 1 hour after triggering.

effect: Any creature that starts its turn in the boiling water must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw, taking 21 (6d6) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The scalding heat lasts for 1 hour, after which the vents return to their normal illumination and the water temperature changes from boiling hot to bearably warm.
area: The water in the chamber up to a height of 30 feet
description: Natural vents spew red light and jets of bubbling water. Removing the ruidium items triggers a flood of boiling-hot water.

name: Ruidium Tendrils (Apotheon's Fury)
trigger: When all three serpentmaws in area N13 are dead, dozens of tendrils of ruidium emerge from the statues in the cavern.

detection.detail: The tendrils emerge automatically after the serpentmaws are killed.

disarm.detail: The tendrils persist for 1 minute, after which they recede back into the statues.

effect: Any creature that enters the cavern or starts its turn there must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or be grappled by a tendril (escape DC 15). While grappled in this way, a creature is also restrained. No more than one tendril can grapple a single creature. Each tendril is an Ooze that has AC 15; 10 hit points; immunity to all damage except slashing; Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution scores of 20; and Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores of 1. A tendril reduced to 0 hit points disintegrates in a crimson haze. On initiative count 0, each creature grappled by a tendril takes 3 (1d6) piercing damage and 3 (1d6) psychic damage as it is flung against one of the cavern's ruidium spikes. The creature remains grappled after taking this damage; in addition, it must succeed on a DC 20 Charisma saving throw or gain 1 level of exhaustion. If the creature is not already suffering from ruidium corruption, it becomes corrupted when it fails the saving throw.
description: When the serpentmaws are killed, ruidium tendrils emerge from statues, grappling and flinging creatures against spikes.

name: East Door Trap
trigger: The first time the door is touched

detection.detail: The door gives off a flash of crimson light when touched.

disarm.detail: A character can use an action to try to pick the lock with thieves' tools, doing so with a successful DC 22 Dexterity check. A knock spell or similar magic also opens the door.

effect: Any creature within 10 feet of the door when this happens must succeed on a DC 18 Strength saving throw or be pushed 20 feet away from the door- and into the death embrace's tentacles, if that creature is still alive and present.
description: A sturdy cellar door with a built-in lock that triggers a crimson flash and pushes creatures away when first touched.

name: Gravity Funnel
trigger: Entering or being within the area

detection.detail: A 10-foot-tall and 10-foot-diameter area of altered gravity.

disarm.detail: Cannot be disarmed.

effect: Strength checks made within a gravity funnel have disadvantage. A ranged weapon attack made through or within a gravity funnel automatically misses a target beyond the weapon's normal range. Creatures and objects that are fully contained within a gravity funnel have resistance against force damage. The gravity funnel counts as difficult terrain.
description: A 10-foot-tall and 10-foot-diameter area of altered gravity that imposes disadvantage on Strength checks, causes ranged attacks to miss beyond normal range, grants resistance to force damage, and counts as difficult terrain.

name: Psychic Miasma
trigger: A creature enters the cloud or starts its turn there

detection.detail: A virtually imperceptible mist of preternatural psychotropic vapor hovers above the ground.

disarm.detail: Cannot be disarmed.

effect: Creatures that are fully immersed in psychic miasma have vulnerability to psychic damage. Any creature that enters a cloud of psychic miasma or starts its turn there must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or become afflicted with a random form of long-term madness (see 'Madness' in chapter 8 of the Dungeon Master's Guide). Creatures that can't be poisoned automatically succeed on the saving throw. A creature that successfully saves against the psychic miasma is immune to its effects for 24 hours. An undead creature that spends at least 1 minute in a cloud of psychic miasma gains advantage on ability checks and saving throws for 24 hours.
description: A virtually imperceptible mist of preternatural psychotropic vapor that corrupts the sanity of the living and fortifies the grim resolve of the undead.

name: Rust Rain
trigger: Exposure to the rain (starting a turn in it or object being exposed)

detection.detail: Crimson precipitation.

disarm.detail: Cannot be disarmed; can be avoided by covering (umbrella, shield, or other rain protection).

effect: Rust rain corrodes nonmagical, ferrous metal objects. If the object isn't being worn or carried, the rain destroys 1 cubic foot of it for every 10 minutes of exposure. An object must be covered to avoid exposure. If the exposed object is nonmagical metal armor, a nonmagical metal weapon, or a nonmagical metal shield being worn or carried, it takes a permanent and cumulative -1 penalty to damage rolls or the AC it offers for every 10 minutes of exposure to rust rain. A weapon that drops to a -5 penalty, armor reduced to an AC of 10, or a shield that drops to a +0 bonus is destroyed. Any creature that starts its turn in rust rain and isn't covered by an umbrella, a shield, or some other form of rain protection takes 1d4 acid damage.
description: Crimson precipitation corrosive to ferrous metal and caustic to creatures.

name: Toxic Fungus Colony
trigger: A non-plant creature comes within 20 feet of the colony

detection.detail: A virulent expanse of malignant fungal growths blankets the landscape.

disarm.detail: Cannot be disarmed.

effect: Any non-plant creature within 20 feet of a toxic fungus colony is poisoned. A creature poisoned by the colony for 1 hour has a 20 percent chance of gaining a random form of short-term madness (see 'Madness' in chapter 8 of the Dungeon Master's Guide). A toxic fungus colony can be bioluminescent. A bioluminescent colony sheds dim light within its area and for an additional 20 feet beyond its outer edges.
description: A virulent expanse of malignant fungal growths that poisons creatures and can cause madness.

name: Volatile Materials Storage Explosion
trigger: Any open flame brought into the area (including that of a torch), as well as any fire or lightning-based effect used in the area, has a 30 percent chance of detonating the materials stored here.

detection.detail: Any character with a passive Wisdom (Perception) score of 13 or higher, or who succeeds on a DC 13 Wisdom (Perception) check, notices that the materials are stored unsafely and assesses that it's a miracle none of it has exploded yet.

effect: This detonation deals 4d10 bludgeoning damage to each creature within the room and in the armory (area L2). It also partially collapses this cavern and alerts every creature within the lair to the characters' intrusion.
area: Within the room and in the armory (area L2)
description: This cavern is extremely dangerous. Any open flame brought into the area (including that of a torch), as well as any fire or lightning-based effect used in the area, has a 30 percent chance of detonating the materials stored here.

name: Kitchen Fire
trigger: A creature that enters the fire for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there

detection.detail: A smoky fire heats the cauldron.

effect: A creature that enters the fire for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there takes 3 (1d6) fire damage.
description: A smoky fire heats the cauldron.

name: Cauldron Fire
trigger: A creature enters the fire for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there

detection.detail: Visible fire

disarm.detail: No disarm method described

effect: A creature that enters the fire for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there takes 3 (1d6) fire damage.
description: A smoky fire heats the cauldron. A creature that enters the fire for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there takes fire damage.

name: Iron Floor Trap (Shark Chamber)
trigger: More than 50 pounds of weight is placed on the iron floor

detection.detail: A character notices that the iron floor is set with a groove at its center, bisecting it lengthwise.

disarm.detail: No disarm method described

effect: The iron floor splits open and its two halves swing down, revealing a 10-foot-deep pool of water 5 feet below where three hungry reef sharks are waiting. The floor resets automatically, snapping shut after being open for 1 minute. Each creature standing on the iron floor when it opens must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw to grab onto the wall and avoid tumbling into the water below. A creature can try to avoid falling into the shark-infested pool by staying close to the wall; it must succeed on a DC 10 Strength (Athletics) check for every 10 feet it moves or tumble into the pool.
area: Iron floor, 40 feet long and 20 feet wide
description: A trap door floor that opens into a shark-infested pool when weight is placed on it.

name: Chest Trap (Ambassador's Bedroom)
trigger: Opening the chest without using the key after the lock is picked

detection.detail: The chest is trapped, which can be noted with a successful DC 14 Intelligence (Investigation) check.

disarm.detail: The trap can be disabled with thieves' tools and a successful DC 14 Dexterity check.

effect: Opening the chest causes a loud shrieking noise to blare for 3 rounds, alerting creatures in areas L9 and L11 if they have not already been dealt with. Opening the chest with the key doesn't trigger the trap.
description: A trapped chest that emits a loud shrieking noise when opened without the key.

name: Steam Trap
trigger: Both sets of double doors swing shut and lock tight once all the characters (or a majority of the characters if some are hanging back) have entered, and Stahlmast has been alerted to their presence.

detection.detail: The holes in the walls extend 1 foot in, then angle downward, preventing the mechanisms of the trap from being seen.

disarm.detail: If all four steam holes are plugged up with cloth or some similar material, the trap stops dealing damage.

effect: With the doors locked, Stahlmast taunts the characters via the speaking tube in the ceiling before filling the chamber with scalding hot steam from the holes in the wall plates. Each creature that starts its turn in the steam takes 2 (1d4) fire damage.
description: A steam trap in a diamond-shaped cavern that fills with scalding steam when triggered, dealing fire damage to creatures that start their turn in the area.

name: Fire Hazards (brazier and fireplace)
trigger: Any creature that comes into contact with the brazier or the fireplace for the first time on its turn, or that starts its turn there

detection.detail: Visible fire sources

disarm.detail: Avoiding contact

effect: Takes 2 (1d4) fire damage
description: Any creature that comes into contact with the brazier or the fireplace for the first time on its turn, or that starts its turn there, takes 2 (1d4) fire damage.

name: Frigid Pool
trigger: A creature completely submerged in a pool

detection.detail: The pool is murky and frigid; characters can see it.

disarm.detail: No disarm; avoid submersion.

effect: A creature completely submerged in a pool must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or gain one level of exhaustion. Creatures with resistance or immunity to cold damage automatically succeed on this saving throw. For each minute the creature spends submerged in a pool, it must repeat this saving throw, gaining another level of exhaustion on a failure.
description: Pools of murky, frigid water within the caverns are created by melting snow on the rocky ground above dripping down through the ceiling.

name: Pit Trap (under bedroll)
trigger: Walking across the bedroll covering the pit

detection.detail: The trap can be spotted with a DC 10 Wisdom (Perception) check.

effect: Anyone walking across the bedroll falls into the pit, taking 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage and landing prone. A creature that falls into the pit makes enough noise that the bandits in area C2 investigate.
description: A pit trap hidden under a bedroll in the bandit camp.

name: Stone Chest Trap
trigger: When a creature touches the chest without speaking a prayer to Tiamat, a gust of wind escapes the dragon's mouth. If the blue powder is still in the dragon's mouth, it forms a cloud that fills a 15-foot cube in front of the chest.

detection.detail: A character who examines the chest and succeeds on a DC 12 Wisdom (Perception) check finds pin-sized openings in the dragon's mouth that contain a blue powder.

disarm.detail: The powder can be removed with a successful DC 15 Dexterity check using thieves' tools. A character who fails this check must succeed on a DC 11 Constitution saving throw or contract frigid woe.

effect: Each creature within the 15-foot cube area must succeed on a DC 11 Constitution saving throw or contract frigid woe.
area: 15-foot cube in front of the chest
description: A stone chest with a dragon face carved on its lid, containing pin-sized openings in the dragon's mouth that hold a blue powder. When touched without a prayer to Tiamat, a gust of wind releases the powder as a cloud.

name: Cold Energy Beam Trap (Chest)
trigger: When a creature makes a failed attempt to pick the chest's lock, or attacks or attempts to force the chest open

detection.detail: A character who searches the exterior of either chest and succeeds on a DC 13 Wisdom (Perception) check finds an archaic Draconic word for 'ice' carved in tiny letters near the hinges. With a successful DC 10 Intelligence (Arcana) check, a character senses that the inscription is connected to a trap.

disarm.method: Intelligence (Arcana) or scratching out the inscription with a tool or weapon
disarm.detail: Scratching out the inscription with a tool or a weapon causes the trap to stop functioning on that chest.

effect: The chest shoots a beam of cold energy at the creature.
description: A magical trap on a stone chest that fires a beam of cold energy when triggered.

name: Flame Hazard (Iron Lever)
trigger: A creature pulls the iron lever down (as an action)

detection.detail: A character who examines the lever notices spots of faded red paint on it with a successful DC 13 Wisdom (Perception) check.

disarm.method: Push the lever back up (as an action)
disarm.detail: A creature can use an action to push the lever back up, which shuts off the flames.

effect: Flames shoot down from the ceiling in area S5.
description: A lever-controlled flame hazard that shoots fire from the ceiling in area S5.

name: Trapped Door
trigger: When a creature makes a failed attempt to pick the door's lock, or attacks or attempts to force the door open

detection.detail: A character who searches the door and succeeds on a DC 13 Intelligence (Investigation) check finds an archaic Draconic word for 'disappear' carved in tiny letters near the foot of the door on both sides.

disarm.method: Intelligence (Arcana) or scratching out the inscription
disarm.detail: With a successful DC 10 Intelligence (Arcana) check, a character senses that the inscription is connected to a trap. Scratching out either inscription with a tool or a weapon causes the trap to stop functioning.

effect: That creature is teleported into the middle of area S15.
description: A magical trap on a locked door that teleports a creature to area S15 when triggered.

name: Wall of Flame (Area S5)
trigger: A creature enters this area or starts its turn there while the flames are active

detection.detail: If the flames aren't active, a character who succeeds on a DC 13 Wisdom (Perception) check notes a faint oily smell in the room and notices pin-sized holes covering the ceiling.

disarm.method: A creature can use an action to push the lever back up, which shuts off the flames.
disarm.detail: A creature can use an action to push the lever back up, which shuts off the flames.

effect: Each creature that enters this area or starts its turn there must make a DC 12 Dexterity saving throw, taking 4 (1d8) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
description: A wall of roiling flame that shoots down from the ceiling, dealing fire damage to creatures in the area.

name: Bear Trap
trigger: A character steps on a bear trap hidden in tall grass. Characters who don't spot the traps have a 50 percent chance of stepping on a bear trap and triggering it whenever they move through the area.

detection.detail: A character with a passive Wisdom (Perception) score of 12 or higher is able to spot the traps and avoid them.

disarm.detail: A successful DC 10 Dexterity check using thieves' tools disables a bear trap.

effect: A bear trap's attack is +8 to hit and deals 5 (1d10) piercing damage on a hit. This attack can't be made with advantage or disadvantage. A creature hit by the trap also has its speed reduced to 0 and can't move until it breaks free of the trap. Breaking free requires a successful DC 15 Strength check by the trapped creature or another creature within 5 feet of the trap.
description: Scores of bear traps are hidden among the tall grass in a 40-foot-wide area surrounding the palisade.

name: Spiked Barricade
trigger: Any Large or bigger creature that moves through an area of spiked barricades.

detection.detail: Visually formidable, these barricades built of crossed rows of spiked poles are obvious.

disarm.detail: No disarm method described; the area is difficult terrain.

effect: Any Large or bigger creature that moves through an area of spiked barricades must succeed on a DC 14 Dexterity saving throw or take 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.
area: Any area containing a spiked barricade
description: Though visually formidable, these barricades built of crossed rows of spiked poles pose a threat only to Large and larger creatures. Any area containing a spiked barricade is difficult terrain.

name: Poisoned Needle Trap
trigger: A character attempts to open the locked wooden chest without disarming the trap.

detection.detail: Any character who examines the chest and succeeds on a DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check discovers a poisoned needle hidden in the chest's lock.

disarm.detail: The needle can be removed with a successful DC 15 Dexterity check using thieves' tools.

effect: On a failed check to remove the needle, the character attempting to remove the needle takes 1 piercing damage and 7 (2d6) poison damage, and must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned for 1 hour.
description: A poisoned needle hidden in the lock of a wooden chest.

name: Glyph of Warding Trap
trigger: The first time the statuette is removed from the pedestal by a creature that is not wearing a holy symbol of Umberlee.

detection.detail: A character who studies the statuette and succeeds on a DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check spots the nearly invisible glyph, which is inscribed on the trident.

disarm.detail: Not specified; presumably dispel magic or similar.

effect: The glyph erupts with magical energy in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on it. Each creature in the area must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 22 (5d8) thunder damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
description: A glyph of warding spell inscribed on the trident of a wooden statuette of Umberlee, triggered when removed by someone not wearing her holy symbol.

name: Crusher Trap
trigger: When a creature enters the 20-foot-square area south of the double door in area 18.

detection.detail: Characters who brush away the dust also find bloodstains and deep scratches on the floor. A character standing north or south of the trapped area can discern, by looking at the scratches on the floor, that the walls are movable blocks of stone, but there’s no way to identify the trap’s trigger or the method of bypassing it without experimentation or the use of divination magic.

disarm.detail: Only a creature wearing a holy symbol of Umberlee can move through the area without triggering the trap.

effect: Giant spring-loaded gears hidden in the walls cause blocks of stone on either side of the hall to slam together. A creature between the colliding blocks of stone must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw. On a success, the creature leaps out of the way in whichever direction it prefers, north or south. On a failed save, the creature takes 44 (8d10) bludgeoning damage. A creature reduced to 0 hit points by this damage is crushed to a pulp. After they slam shut, the blocks take 1 minute to retract into the walls, whereupon the trap resets.
area: 20-foot-square area south of the double door in area 18
description: A mechanical trap with a magical sensor that causes stone blocks to slam together when a creature enters the area.

name: Teleportation/Lightning Orb
trigger: Whenever a creature touches the orb in area 17.

detection.detail: The orb radiates an aura of conjuration magic under the scrutiny of a detect magic spell or similar effect.

disarm.detail: The orb can’t be removed from its wall fixture. It has AC 10, 1 hit point, and immunity to poison and psychic damage. Destroying the orb extinguishes its light and renders the pieces nonmagical.

effect: Whenever a creature touches the orb, roll a d6. On a roll of 2 or higher, the orb teleports the creature to area 24. On a roll of 1, the orb malfunctions and emits lightning in a 100-foot-long line as wide as the hall. Each creature in the area of effect must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 14 (4d6) lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
area: 100-foot-long line as wide as the hall
description: A crystal orb that teleports creatures or emits lightning when touched.

name: Mud Pit Portal
trigger: An open flame is burning within 10 feet of a mud pit, and a creature fully submerges itself in the pit.

detection.detail: A detect magic spell reveals a faint aura of abjuration magic around each pool.

disarm.detail: Removing the open flame from within 10 feet of the pit deactivates the portal.

effect: The creature is transported to a similar mud pit on the Elemental Plane of Earth.
area: Each mud pit is 5 feet deep, 50 feet wide, and roughly circular.
description: Three pools of mud heated by geothermal vents that serve as portals to the Elemental Plane of Earth when an open flame is nearby.

name: Collapsing Roof
trigger: Trip wire is pulled or support beams are knocked over

detection.detail: Spotting the trip wire 3 inches off the ground between two support beams. Anyone inspecting the beams can tell they're merely wedged in place.

disarm.detail: Disables the trip wire harmlessly. A character without thieves' tools can attempt with disadvantage using any edged weapon or tool. On a failed check, the trap triggers.

effect: The unstable ceiling collapses. Any creature in the area beneath must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 22 (4d10) bludgeoning damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. The floor becomes difficult terrain.
description: A trip wire stretched between two support beams keeps an unstable section of ceiling in place. When triggered, the ceiling collapses.

name: Falling Net
trigger: Trip wire is pulled

detection.detail: Spotting the trip wire and the net hidden by cobwebs or foliage.

disarm.detail: Breaking the trip wire harmlessly. Without thieves' tools, attempt with disadvantage using any edged weapon. On a failed check, the trap triggers.

effect: The net drops, covering a 10-foot-square area. Creatures in the area are trapped under the net and restrained, and those that fail a DC 10 Strength saving throw are also knocked prone. A creature can use its action to make a DC 10 Strength check to free itself or another. The net has AC 10 and 20 hit points; dealing 5 slashing damage destroys a 5-foot section.
description: A trip wire releases a net suspended from the ceiling, trapping creatures beneath it.

name: Fire-Breathing Statue
trigger: More than 20 pounds of weight placed on a hidden pressure plate

detection.detail: Spotting the pressure plate and faint scorch marks on the floor and walls. Detect magic reveals an aura of evocation magic around the statue.

disarm.detail: Wedging an iron spike or other object under the pressure plate prevents activation. A successful dispel magic (DC 13) cast on the statue destroys the trap.

effect: The statue releases a 30-foot cone of fire. Each creature in the cone must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw, taking 22 (4d10) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one.
description: A statue (such as a dragon or wizard) releases a magical gout of flame when a hidden pressure plate is depressed.

name: Simple Pit
trigger: Stepping on the cloth cover

detection.detail: Spotting the pit covered by a large cloth anchored on the edge and camouflaged with dirt and debris.

disarm.detail: The pit can be uncovered and avoided once detected.

effect: Anyone stepping on the cloth falls through and takes falling damage based on the pit's depth (usually 10 feet, 1d6 bludgeoning per 10 feet).
description: A hole dug in the ground, covered by a large cloth anchored on the pit's edge and camouflaged with dirt and debris.

name: Hidden Pit
trigger: Stepping on the pit's cover

detection.detail: Discerns an absence of foot traffic over the section of floor that forms the pit's cover. A successful DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check confirms the trapped section is actually the cover of a pit.

disarm.detail: An iron spike or similar object can be wedged between the pit's cover and the surrounding floor to prevent it from opening. The cover can also be magically held shut with arcane lock or similar magic.

effect: When a creature steps on the cover, it swings open like a trapdoor, causing the intruder to fall into the pit below. The pit is usually 10 or 20 feet deep but can be deeper.
description: A pit with a cover constructed from material identical to the surrounding floor.

name: Locking Pit
trigger: Stepping on the pit's cover

detection.detail: Same as a hidden pit — absence of foot traffic over the cover.

disarm.detail: A successful DC 20 Strength check is necessary to pry the cover open. The cover can also be smashed open. A character in the pit can attempt to disable the spring mechanism from the inside with a DC 15 Dexterity check using thieves' tools.

effect: Identical to a hidden pit trap, except the spring-loaded cover snaps shut after a creature falls in, trapping the victim inside.
description: A hidden pit trap with a spring-loaded cover that snaps shut after a creature falls in, trapping the victim inside.

name: Spiked Pit
trigger: Stepping on the pit's cover

detection.detail: A successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check spots the trap, with a DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check to confirm.

disarm.detail: Provided the mechanism can be reached, a successful DC 15 Dexterity check using thieves' tools disarms the trap. In some cases, a mechanism behind a secret door nearby opens the pit safely.

effect: A creature falling into the pit takes 11 (2d10) piercing damage from the spikes at the bottom, in addition to any falling damage. If poison is smeared on the spikes, the creature must also make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw, taking 22 (4d10) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one.
description: A pit trap with sharpened wooden or iron spikes at the bottom, possibly coated with poison.

name: Poison Darts
trigger: More than 20 pounds of weight placed on a hidden pressure plate

detection.detail: Spotting tiny holes in the walls obscured by dust, cobwebs, or hidden amid bas-reliefs. A DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check deduces the pressure plate from variations in mortar and stone.

disarm.detail: Wedging an iron spike under the pressure plate prevents activation. Stuffing the holes with cloth or wax prevents the darts from launching.

effect: Four darts shoot from spring-loaded tubes in the walls. Each dart makes a ranged attack with a +8 bonus against a random target within 10 feet of the pressure plate. A target hit takes 2 (1d4) piercing damage and must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw, taking 11 (2d10) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one.
description: Poison-tipped darts shoot from spring-loaded tubes hidden in the walls when a pressure plate is stepped on.

name: Poison Needle
trigger: Opening a chest or lock without the proper key

detection.detail: Deducing the trap's presence from alterations made to the lock to accommodate the needle.

disarm.detail: A successful DC 15 Dexterity check using thieves' tools removes the needle from the lock. Unsuccessfully attempting to pick the lock triggers the trap.

effect: The needle extends 3 inches from the lock. A creature within range takes 1 piercing damage and 11 (2d10) poison damage, and must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned for 1 hour.
description: A poisoned needle hidden within a treasure chest's lock springs out when opened without the proper key.

name: Rolling Sphere
trigger: More than 20 pounds of pressure on a hidden pressure plate

detection.detail: Spotting the trapdoor in the ceiling and the pressure plate on the floor. A DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check reveals variations in mortar betraying the pressure plate and trapdoor.

disarm.detail: Wedging an iron spike or other object under the pressure plate prevents activation. As an action, a creature within 5 feet of the sphere can attempt a DC 20 Strength check to slow it, reducing speed by 15 feet. If speed drops to 0, it stops.

effect: A 10-foot-diameter rolling sphere of solid stone drops from the ceiling. The sphere rolls initiative with a +8 bonus, moving 60 feet per turn in a straight line. It can move through creatures' spaces (difficult terrain). A creature whose space the sphere enters must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or take 55 (10d10) bludgeoning damage and be knocked prone. The sphere stops when it hits a wall.
description: A massive stone sphere rolls from a trapdoor in the ceiling, crushing creatures in its path.

name: Sphere of Annihilation
trigger: Entering the stone face's mouth or touching the sphere

detection.detail: Reveals that the mouth contains a sphere of annihilation that can't be controlled or moved. The mouth is 2 feet in diameter, filled with impenetrable magical darkness from which no sound issues.

disarm.detail: A successful dispel magic (DC 18) removes the enchantment. The sphere of annihilation itself cannot be dispelled and remains.

effect: Any matter that enters the mouth is instantly obliterated, identical to a normal sphere of annihilation. Some versions include a sympathy enchantment causing specified creatures to feel an overwhelming urge to approach and crawl inside.
description: A stone face carved into a wall with a mouth containing a sphere of annihilation. Magical darkness fills the mouth, and any matter that enters is instantly obliterated.

name: Concealed Pit Trap
trigger: A creature crosses the hidden trapdoor in the mud-and-debris-covered floor

detection.detail: Spotting the concealed trapdoor is at disadvantage due to mud and debris covering the area.

disarm.detail: A narrow ledge remains around the pit after it opens, allowing passage.

effect: The floor opens into a 20-foot-deep pit. A creature falling in takes 7 (2d6) bludgeoning damage.
description: A 20-foot-deep pit trap in Dungrunglung, concealed by mud and debris. Spotting it is at disadvantage.

name: Blade Trap
trigger: A creature enters the 10-foot-square corridor

detection.detail: The blades are concealed in wall niches and are not visible until triggered.

disarm.detail: Can be jammed with 4 successful DC 10 Strength checks.

effect: Scything blades sweep from concealed wall niches in a 10-foot-square corridor. Each creature in the area must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw, taking 18 (4d8) slashing damage on a failure, or half as much on a success.
description: Scything blades sweep from concealed wall niches in a 10-foot-square corridor in Dungrunglung.

name: Rolling Stone Trap
trigger: A tripwire across a tunnel mouth is disturbed

detection.detail: Spotting the tripwire across the tunnel mouth.

disarm.detail: A successful check disconnects the tripwire without triggering the trap.

effect: A spring-loaded claw snaps across the tunnel, releasing a rolling boulder. Any creature in the tunnel must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or take 22 (4d10) bludgeoning damage.
area: The tunnel mouth and corridor beyond
description: A tripwire in Wyrmheart Mine triggers a spring-loaded claw that releases a rolling boulder down the tunnel.

name: Spring Trap (Yellyark)
trigger: The holding vine of the bent-down tree is cut

detection.detail: Noticing the bent tree held by a vine and recognizing the goblin village sits atop it.

disarm.detail: Carefully releasing the tension on the vine without cutting it.

effect: The bent-down tree launches upward, hurling everything on it. Creatures in the goblin village take 28 (8d6) bludgeoning damage on impact.
area: The entire goblin village of Yellyark
description: The goblin village of Yellyark sits atop a bent-down tree acting as a gigantic spring trap. Cutting the holding vine launches the village.

name: Unkh's Shrine Trap (Flail Snail Statue)
trigger: Inserting the wrong key into the lock or failing a lockpick check

detection.detail: Examining the flail snail statue reveals arcane glyphs and the keyhole's mechanism.

disarm.detail: Carefully picking the lock without triggering the magical trap.

effect: The flail snail statue emits devastating rays of light. All creatures in the shrine must make a DC 18 Dexterity saving throw, taking 33 (6d10) radiant damage on a failure, or half as much on a success.
description: In the Shrine of Unkh in Omu, inserting the wrong key causes the flail snail statue to emit devastating rays of light.

name: Poison Darts (I'jin's Shrine)
trigger: Stepping on the wrong animal-themed tiles

detection.detail: Spotting the tiny holes in the wall where darts emerge and noticing the animal tile pattern.

disarm.detail: Deducing the tile pattern: never stepping on the same animal type twice avoids triggering the trap.

effect: Four poison darts fire from wall holes. Each dart: +5 to hit, 2 piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) poison damage (DC 15 Constitution halves the poison). Avoidable by never stepping on the same animal design twice in a row.
area: The room with animal-themed floor tiles
description: In the Shrine of I'jin in Omu, stepping on wrong animal-themed tiles triggers four poisoned darts from wall holes.

name: Puzzle Cube Trap (Obo'laka's Shrine)
trigger: Attempting to take the puzzle cube without properly positioning the torches

detection.detail: Examining the magic torches and the brackets in the Gallery of Carvings reveals the puzzle mechanism.

disarm.detail: The torches must be placed in the correct brackets in the Gallery of Carvings (area 19B) to disarm the trap and safely claim the puzzle cube.

effect: Magic torches power a trap that activates when the puzzle cube is disturbed without following the proper ritual. The exact effect depends on how the torches are positioned.
description: In Obo'laka's shrine in Omu, magic torches power a trap guarding one of the nine puzzle cubes. The torches must be placed in brackets in the correct order.

name: Poison Needle (Fane of the Night Serpent)
trigger: Opening the locked south door without disarming the needle

detection.detail: Spotting the tiny needle hidden in the lock mechanism.

disarm.detail: A successful DC 12 Dexterity check disables the needle without triggering it.

effect: A hidden poison needle springs from the lock. The target takes 5 (1d10) piercing damage and must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned and become permanently blinded. Lesser restoration cures the blindness.
description: A hidden poison needle in the lock of the south door in the Fane of the Night Serpent causes permanent blindness on a failed save.

name: Pit Trap (False Entrance)
trigger: A lever at the False Entrance puzzle door area is pulled

detection.detail: Examining the floor reveals it is a false surface designed to split open.

disarm.detail: Jamming the floor mechanism prevents it from opening.

effect: The floor splits into a 20-foot-deep pit lined with poisoned spikes. A falling creature takes 11 (2d10) bludgeoning damage plus spike damage and must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned for 24 hours.
area: The floor at the False Entrance puzzle door
description: A lever-operated pit trap at the False Entrance to the Tomb of the Nine Gods, lined with poisoned spikes.

name: Trapped Corridor (Caustic Gas)
trigger: The puzzle door seals the tunnel with creatures inside

detection.detail: Examining the bas-relief bearded devil face reveals small openings in the skull mouths for gas release.

disarm.detail: A successful dispel magic (DC 16) or plugging the skull mouths prevents the gas from releasing.

effect: A bas-relief bearded devil face on the wall releases caustic gas from its skull mouths. Creatures in the corridor must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or take 5 poison damage plus 5 acid damage each round for 10 rounds.
damage: 5 poison + 5 acid per round for 10 rounds
area: The mossy corridor beyond the False Entrance
description: A magical trap in the Tomb of the Nine Gods that releases caustic gas from a bearded devil bas-relief when the corridor is sealed.

name: Poison Darts (Area 5A)
trigger: 20+ pounds of pressure on one of the marked pressure plates

detection.detail: Spotting the tiny holes in the wall tubes and the slightly raised pressure plates on the floor.

disarm.detail: Disabling the pressure plate mechanism prevents the darts from firing.

effect: Poison-tipped darts fire from wall tubes. Each crossbow-like dart: +8 to hit, 2 piercing damage plus 14 (4d6) poison damage (DC 15 Constitution halves the poison). Each marked X on the map corresponds to a pressure plate.
area: Multiple pressure-plate-triggered dart traps in the corridor
description: Poison-tipped darts fire from wall tubes in the Tomb of the Nine Gods, triggered by pressure plates marked on the dungeon map.

name: Trapped Chest (Demon Skull)
trigger: Failing a DC 22 lockpick check by 5 or more

detection.detail: Examining the demon skull keyhole reveals a faint teleportation enchantment.

disarm.detail: Successfully picking the DC 22 lock without failing by 5 or more.

effect: The character is teleported inside the locked chest, which dangles 30 feet above water. The character is restrained and begins suffocating inside the chest until freed from outside.
area: A dangling treasure chest with a demon skull keyhole
description: A dangling treasure chest in the Tomb of the Nine Gods teleports those who badly fail a lockpick attempt inside itself, where they begin suffocating.

name: Wine Flood Trap (False Tomb)
trigger: Opening the gilded coffin in sunlight

detection.detail: Examining the coffin reveals its connection to the ceiling gargoyles and the stone block sealing mechanism.

disarm.detail: Wedging the stone block mechanism before opening the coffin prevents it from sealing the entrance. Destroying or covering the gargoyle heads prevents wine flow.

effect: A stone block seals the entrance, then four gargoyle heads flood the room with wine at 1 foot per round. Three wine weirds attack. The room is fully flooded after 12 rounds. The trap resets at dawn.
description: Opening the gilded coffin in the False Tomb of the Tomb of the Nine Gods seals the room and floods it with wine, summoning wine weirds.

name: Revolving Room Trap
trigger: A tomb guardian pulls a lever, causing the cylindrical room to revolve

detection.detail: Examining the cylindrical room reveals rotating joints and concealed hazard vents.

disarm.detail: Jamming the lever mechanism prevents the room from revolving.

effect: The cylindrical room revolves rapidly. Creatures inside take 11 (2d10) bludgeoning damage each turn (DC 15 Dexterity halves). Each round, roll on a d20 table for an additional effect: sleep gas, blinding dust, flame jets, or force damage. The room contains beholder-vault keys.
description: A cylindrical room in the Tomb of the Nine Gods that revolves when a lever is pulled, dealing bludgeoning damage and random hazardous effects.

name: Lava Trap (Fire Cell)
trigger: Touching or removing the candle in the Elemental Cells puzzle

detection.detail: Recognizing the magical runes in the ceiling and the antimagic field suppressing magical protections.

disarm.detail: Extinguishing the candle teleports all occupants to another elemental cell. The trap cannot be disarmed normally.

effect: Lava rains from holes in the ceiling. Creatures must make a DC 20 Dexterity saving throw each turn or take 22 (4d10) fire damage. An antimagic field prevents magical fire resistance. The trap continues until the candle is extinguished.
description: In the Tomb of the Nine Gods' Elemental Cells, touching the candle causes lava to rain from the ceiling. Antimagic field prevents magical protection.

name: Flood Trap (Water Cell)
trigger: Entering the Water Cell of the Elemental Cells puzzle

detection.detail: Noticing the water level slowly rising and the oysters and snails that provide escape.

disarm.detail: Eating an oyster or snail teleports the creature to another elemental cell. Being the last to leave the cell also teleports the creature.

effect: Water fills the cell at 1 foot per round, fully flooding it in 10 rounds. An antimagic field prevents water breathing magic. Creatures can escape by eating an oyster or snail (teleports to another cell) or being the last to leave.
description: In the Tomb of the Nine Gods' Elemental Cells, water fills the room at 1 ft/round. Antimagic field prevents magical water breathing.

name: Sand Trap (Earth Cell)
trigger: Entering the Earth Cell of the Elemental Cells puzzle

detection.detail: Examining the floor reveals the split mechanism and the giant stone grinders below.

disarm.detail: A button somewhere in the room stops the rollers. Antimagic field prevents magical solutions.

effect: Sand falls at 6 inches per round, making difficult terrain. At 12 inches depth, the floor splits open into a pit with two giant stone grinders dealing 132 (24d10) force damage to anything caught in them. An antimagic field is active.
description: In the Tomb of the Nine Gods' Elemental Cells, sand fills the room until the floor opens into a pit with giant stone grinders.

name: Spider Fan Trap (Hag's Nursery)
trigger: Reading a nursery rhyme book aloud or opening a secret compartment

detection.detail: Examining the book reveals it is enchanted with a reverse gravity spell connected to the ceiling.

disarm.detail: The trap does not reset and triggers only once. It lasts 1 minute.

effect: A reverse gravity effect activates. Creatures fall upward through a false plaster ceiling into a rotating iron spider fan, taking 44 (8d10) slashing damage each round. The effect lasts 1 minute and does not reset.
description: A magical trap in the Tomb of the Nine Gods that flips gravity upward into a rotating iron spider fan when a nursery rhyme book is read aloud.

name: Snare (Goblin Trail)
trigger: A creature walks into the hidden snare on the trail

detection.detail: Spotting the hidden snare on the goblin trail (or passive Perception 12).

disarm.detail: Cutting the cord (1 slashing damage) frees a restrained creature.

effect: The creature is hoisted upside down 10 feet into the air and restrained until 1+ slashing damage cuts the cord. The creature takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage from the fall if not caught.
area: A 10-foot section of the Goblin Trail
description: A hidden snare on the Triboar Trail that hoists creatures upside down into the air.

name: Pit (Goblin Trail)
trigger: A creature moves across the covered pit

detection.detail: Spotting the covered pit on the goblin trail (or passive Perception 15).

disarm.detail: The pit walls are climbable without a check.

effect: The creature falls 10 feet into the pit, taking 1d6 bludgeoning damage. The walls are easy to climb.
area: A 10-foot-deep pit on the Goblin Trail
description: A covered pit along the Triboar Trail, 10 feet deep with climbable walls.

name: Collapsible Ledge (Cragmaw Hideout)
trigger: More than 100 pounds of weight on the escarpment ledge

detection.detail: Noticing the escarpment ledge is unstable and crumbles under heavy weight.

disarm.detail: Avoiding the ledge or distributing weight across a larger surface.

effect: The escarpment ledge collapses. Creatures on it must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or take 2d6 bludgeoning damage and fall prone.
area: The escarpment ledge in Cragmaw Hideout area 4
description: An unstable escarpment ledge in Cragmaw Hideout that collapses under more than 100 pounds of weight.

name: Bridge Collapse (Cragmaw Hideout)
trigger: The bridge is reduced to 0 HP (AC 5, 10 HP)

detection.detail: Examining the bridge reveals it is old and rotten, barely holding together.

disarm.detail: Reinforcing the bridge before crossing or crossing one at a time.

effect: The bridge collapses. Creatures on it fall 20 feet, taking 2d6 bludgeoning damage.
area: The overpass bridge in Cragmaw Hideout area 5
description: A rotten bridge over a 20-foot chasm in Cragmaw Hideout that collapses when damaged.

name: Flood Trap (Cragmaw Hideout)
trigger: Goblins yank collapsible walls to release a water surge

detection.detail: Spotting the collapsible walls and hearing rushing water beyond them.

disarm.detail: Wedging the collapsible walls shut prevents them from opening.

effect: A surge of water sweeps through the chamber. Creatures must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or be swept away and knocked prone, taking 1d6 bludgeoning damage. A DC 15 Strength check allows a creature to hold on.
description: Goblins can release a water surge in Cragmaw Hideout by yanking collapsible walls, sweeping creatures toward area 1.

name: Pit Trap (Redbrand Hideout)
trigger: 100+ pounds of pressure on the false floor (loose stone tiles over breakaway timbers)

detection.detail: Spotting the loose stone tiles that don't match the rest of the floor (or passive Perception 15).

disarm.detail: A narrow ledge around the edges allows passage with a DC 10 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check.

effect: The floor collapses. Creatures fall 20 feet into the pit, taking 2d6 bludgeoning damage and landing prone. A successful DC 15 Dexterity saving throw allows a creature to catch the edge.
area: The trapped hall in Redbrand Hideout area 3
description: A pit trap in the Redbrand Hideout's trapped hall, with breakaway timbers over a 20-foot pit.

name: Collapsing Bridge (Redbrand Hideout)
trigger: A creature weighing 50+ lbs moves across the south bridge

detection.detail: Spotting the faulty construction and sabotage in the bridge supports.

disarm.detail: Reinforcing the bridge supports before crossing.

effect: The bridge drops into a 20-foot crevasse. Creatures on it take 2d6 bludgeoning damage from the fall.
area: The south bridge over the crevasse in Redbrand Hideout area 8
description: A sabotaged bridge in the Redbrand Hideout that collapses under 50+ pounds of weight.

name: Tripwire Cave-In (Cragmaw Castle)
trigger: A creature walks through the rubble without avoiding the copper tripwire

detection.detail: Spotting the copper tripwire in the rubble (or passive Perception 20).

disarm.detail: A successful DC 10 Dexterity check disconnects the tripwire without triggering the cave-in.

effect: Wooden beams and stones collapse from the ceiling. Creatures in the area must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or take 3d6 bludgeoning damage (half on success). The noise alerts monsters in areas 3, 7, 8, and 9.
description: A tripwire-activated cave-in at Cragmaw Castle that collapses wooden beams and stones on intruders.

name: Poison Gas (Wave Echo Cave)
trigger: A creature attempts to cross the fungi-covered cavern

detection.detail: Identifying the fungi as a toxic variety that releases poisonous spores when disturbed.

disarm.detail: The gas disperses after 1 minute. Creatures can wait for it to clear or find an alternate path.

effect: Fungi carpets release poisonous gas. Creatures must succeed on a DC 11 Constitution saving throw or take 3d6 poison damage and become poisoned for 10 minutes. The save repeats each turn spent in the cavern. Gas disperses after 1 minute.
description: A cavern in Wave Echo Cave carpeted with toxic fungi that release poisonous gas when disturbed.

name: Ceiling Collapse (Temple of Dumathoin)
trigger: Removing either emerald eye from the statue

detection.detail: Examining the statue reveals the emerald eyes are integrated into the structural support, and removing them will destabilize the ceiling.

disarm.detail: Prying the emerald eyes loose carefully with a successful DC 10 Strength check. Alternatively, supporting the pillars before removing the eyes.

effect: The pillars crack and the ceiling collapses. Creatures in the temple must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 4d10 bludgeoning damage on a failure, or half as much on a success.
area: Wave Echo Cave area 19 (Temple of Dumathoin)
description: A magical structural trap in Wave Echo Cave where removing the emerald eyes from a statue causes the ceiling to collapse.

name: Bear Traps (Alley)
trigger: Stepping in a muddy puddle concealing a spring-loaded bear trap

detection.detail: Spotting the hidden bear traps in the muddy puddles in the alley (passive Perception 13).

disarm.detail: A successful DC 12 Strength check pries the jaws of the bear trap open.

effect: The bear trap snaps shut. The creature takes 1d6 slashing damage and is restrained. A DC 12 Strength check frees the creature.
description: Five spring-loaded bear traps hidden in muddy puddles in a Waterdeep alley.

name: Glyph of Warding (Explosive Runes)
trigger: Anyone other than Grinda Garloth lifts the lid of her sea chest

detection.detail: Examining the sea chest reveals magical glyphs on the interior of the lid.

disarm.detail: A successful dispel magic (DC 15) removes the glyph.

effect: An explosive runes glyph of warding triggers, dealing force damage to all creatures within 20 feet of the chest. Damage and DC as per the glyph of warding spell.
description: A glyph of warding (explosive runes) placed on Grinda Garloth's sea chest, triggered if anyone other than Grinda opens it.

name: Glyph of Warding (Fire, Mausoleum)
trigger: Stepping on the first step down to the mausoleum underground level

detection.detail: Brushing away the dust covering the glyph on the step.

disarm.detail: A successful dispel magic (DC 15) removes the glyph.

effect: The glyph erupts in fire. Creatures in a 20-foot radius must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 5d8 fire damage on a failure, or half as much on a success.
area: 20-foot radius from the first step to the mausoleum
description: A fire glyph of warding on the first step down to the mausoleum underground level, hidden under dust.

name: Glyph of Warding (Tasha's Hideous Laughter)
trigger: Rooftop chase complication — stepping on the glyph

detection.detail: Spotting the magical glyph on the roof tiles.

disarm.detail: A successful dispel magic (DC 14) removes the glyph.

effect: The target must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw or fall prone under the effect of Tasha's hideous laughter for 1 minute, becoming incapacitated and unable to stand.
description: A glyph of warding (Tasha's hideous laughter) placed on a roof in Waterdeep to discourage burglars.

name: Collapsing Floor (Windmill)
trigger: The first Small or larger creature crosses the upper chamber floor

detection.detail: Noticing the floor is weakened and may collapse under weight.

disarm.detail: Avoiding the upper chamber entirely or reinforcing the floor before crossing.

effect: The floor collapses. Creatures fall 20 feet. Additionally, falling debris deals 4d8 bludgeoning damage (DC 11 Dexterity for half).
area: Upper chamber floor (W4b) of the windmill
description: A weakened upper chamber floor in a windmill that collapses under the first Small+ creature crossing it.

name: Gorm Gulthyn Statue Trap (Fire Eyes)
trigger: Touching the false adamantine trapdoor under the statue

detection.detail: Identifying the statue as Gorm Gulthyn and recognizing the trapdoor as a trap rather than a real exit.

disarm.detail: A DC 17 Religion check to identify the god reveals the nature of the trap and how to avoid triggering it.

effect: Fire rays erupt from the statue's eyes. Creatures in the area must make a DC 18 Dexterity saving throw, taking 4d10 fire damage on a failure, or half as much on a success.
area: Area V8 near the statue of Gorm Gulthyn
description: A false adamantine trapdoor under the statue of Gorm Gulthyn in Waterdeep triggers fire rays from the statue's eyes when touched.

name: Tripwire Collapsing Maze
trigger: A creature trips the wire in Ahmaergo's crate maze (Area X10)

detection.detail: Spotting the tripwire strung across the maze path.

disarm.detail: A successful DC 12 check disconnects the tripwire without triggering the collapse.

effect: The crate maze walls collapse onto creatures in the area. Creatures must succeed on a DC 12 Dexterity saving throw or take 3d6 bludgeoning damage.
area: Xanathar's Lair, Ahmaergo's crate maze (Area X10)
description: A tripwire in Ahmaergo's crate maze in Xanathar's Lair triggers collapsing walls that crush creatures.

name: Green Ray Trap
trigger: Pushing the wizard-eye button on the wall carving

detection.detail: Examining the wall carving reveals a teleportation enchantment in the wizard-eye button.

disarm.detail: A successful dispel magic (DC 16) disables the teleportation effect.

effect: A green ray discharges from the button. The target must make a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw or appear to be disintegrated (actually teleported to a holding cell, area X34).
description: A wall carving in Xanathar's Lair discharges a green ray that teleports creatures to a holding cell, appearing as disintegration.

name: Poison Gas Chest (Cassalanter Villa)
trigger: Opening the treasure box without using the golden key

detection.detail: Examining the box reveals a poison spray mechanism connected to the lock. The golden key is the only safe way to open it.

disarm.detail: The trap cannot be disarmed. The box opens safely only with the golden key.

effect: The box sprays poison gas in a 15-foot radius. Creatures must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or take 4d10 poison damage.
description: A treasure box in Cassalanter Villa (Area C21) that sprays poison gas when opened without the golden key. Cannot be disarmed.

name: Cold Trap (False Vault)
trigger: Entering the false vault (Area C27) without speaking the password 'Gold is my shield'

detection.detail: Examining the ceiling reveals a magical glyph. DC 16 Intelligence (Arcana) identifies it as a cold-based glyph of warding.

disarm.detail: A successful dispel magic (DC 16) targeting the ceiling glyph disables the trap.

effect: Magical cold fills the room. Creatures must succeed on a DC 16 Constitution saving throw or take 8d8 cold damage.
area: The false vault (Area C27) in Cassalanter Villa
description: A magical cold trap in the false vault of Cassalanter Villa. Must speak 'Gold is my shield' to avoid triggering the ceiling glyph.

name: Collapsing Floor (Balcony, Temple of Asmodeus)
trigger: A Medium or larger creature steps onto the weakened balcony

detection.detail: Noticing the balcony floor is crumbling and weakened.

disarm.detail: Reinforcing the balcony floor before crossing.

effect: The balcony floor crumbles. Creatures on it must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or fall 20 feet to the floor below.
area: The balcony (Area A2) in the Temple of Asmodeus
description: A weakened balcony in the Temple of Asmodeus (Cassalanter Villa) that crumbles under Medium+ creatures.

name: Animated Staffs (Kolat Towers)
trigger: Entering Area K12 without Manshoon's escort

detection.detail: Recognizing the staffs as magically animated guardians attuned to Manshoon.

disarm.detail: Having Manshoon's escort allows safe passage. The staffs can be destroyed in combat.

effect: Six staffs animate and attack anyone entering without Manshoon's escort. They have the statistics of flying swords (dealing bludgeoning damage). If not dealt with, they summon help from Area K14.
description: Six animated staffs in Kolat Towers that attack anyone entering without Manshoon's escort.

name: Glyph of Warding (Blindness, Kolat Towers)
trigger: Opening the holding cell door (Area K13) by anyone other than Manshoon

detection.detail: Examining the door reveals a magical glyph of warding.

disarm.detail: A successful dispel magic (DC 18) removes the glyph.

effect: The glyph triggers blindness/deafness on the creature that opened the door. DC 18 Constitution saving throw or be blinded and deafened for the spell's duration.
area: The holding cell door in Kolat Towers Area K13
description: A glyph of warding on a holding cell door in Kolat Towers triggers blindness/deafness when opened by anyone but Manshoon.

name: Floor Clamps (Kolat Towers)
trigger: Pulling the lever in the Construct Workshop (Area K16)

detection.detail: Examining the lever reveals it is connected to a mechanism in the floor and ceiling.

disarm.detail: Disconnecting the lever from the clamp mechanism before pulling it.

effect: Floor clamps lock creatures in place and the floor magically rams upward into the ceiling. Creatures must succeed on a DC 20 Dexterity saving throw or take 4d10 bludgeoning damage.
description: A lever-operated trap in Kolat Towers that clamps creatures to the floor and rams it into the ceiling.

name: Golem Trap (Poison Gas, Kolat Towers)
trigger: The flesh golem steps off its pressure plate (Area K17)

detection.detail: Noticing the pressure plate beneath the flesh golem and the gas vents in the walls.

disarm.detail: Preventing the golem from leaving its pressure plate, or dealing with the golem quickly.

effect: Poison gas erupts from wall holes. Creatures must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution saving throw or take 3d6 poison damage. The save repeats each round while the gas lingers.
description: A flesh golem standing on a pressure plate in Kolat Towers releases poison gas when it steps off.

name: Arcane Rune (Kolat Towers)
trigger: First damage dealt to the rune sustaining Kolat Towers' force field (Area K18)

detection.detail: Identifying the rune as the power source for Kolat Towers' force field.

disarm.detail: A successful dispel magic (DC 19) destroys the rune. It can also be destroyed (AC 10, 22 HP).

effect: The first time the rune takes damage, it summons a red slaad to defend it. The rune sustains the force field protecting Kolat Towers.
description: A magical rune in Kolat Towers that sustains the force field and summons a red slaad when damaged.

name: Spirit Trap (Blackstaff)
trigger: A Blackstaff dies while wielding the Blackstaff legendary staff

detection.detail: Identifying the Blackstaff's enchantment reveals it traps the spirits of its wielders.

disarm.detail: Destroying the Blackstaff releases the trapped spirits.

effect: The spirit of the Blackstaff who dies while wielding the staff is trapped inside. The spirit cannot be raised from the dead while trapped. Destroying the staff releases them.
description: The Blackstaff legendary staff traps the spirit of each Blackstaff who dies while wielding it. Spirits can't be raised while trapped.
